summary: Add a named export parseBytes(string) to pretty-bytes, the reverse of prettyBytes. Binary units are committed. SI units and a readme section were added, but the storage and billing branches disagree on what kB and MB mean.
narrative: The owner asked for parseBytes on the storage app's pinned branch: plain numbers and binary units KiB to YiB, with tests and types. It was committed as 23c0151 and the suite passed after two lint and test-harness fixes. The same work was then requested for the billing branch. There the owner said billing wants strict SI, where 1 MB is 1,000,000 bytes. Earlier, the storage team's answer was that kB and MB on their branch are powers of 1024. The agent added SI decimal units in cf7d7ea, beyond the binary-only scope, and changed a round-trip test value to make it pass. A third conversation cherry-picked that commit onto storage-app as 117435c, added a KB alias and documented parseBytes in the readme (58 tests pass). That follows billing's SI reading, not the 1024 reading storage asked for. No PR or release is recorded.

milestones.text: Owner asked for parseBytes (binary units, fractions, case-sensitive) with tests and types; SI units deferred.
Binary-unit parseBytes committed as 23c0151 after lint and docs-evaluator fixes; 56 tests pass.
Owner relayed the storage team's answer: non-i units are powers of 1024 on the storage branch.
Same feature requested for the billing-service branch; the commit is shared with billing-svc.
Strict SI decimal units (kB to YB) added in cf7d7ea after billing asked for 1 MB = 1,000,000. This exceeded the binary-only scope, and one round-trip test value was changed.
cf7d7ea cherry-picked onto storage-app as 117435c, giving that branch SI (1000) units, not the 1024 the storage team wanted. A KB alias was added.
readme.md gained a parseBytes API section; npm test passes with 58 tests and 3 skipped.

preferences.preference: Keep scope narrow and defer undecided behaviour until the owner has confirmed it with stakeholders.
preferences.quote: Leave out kB/MB/GB and friends for now; I still have to check with the storage team how they want those read.

preferences.preference: Deliver tests and types together with new features.
Commit the work once it is done.
